notes:
FORMS:
Compound verb: ⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ (to strike, to hit) + ⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧ (to raise)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{打|う}ち{上|あ}げる - to launch something (transitive)
- 〜⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{打|う}ち{上|あ}げられる - passive; the usual form in news reports, where the launching organization goes unstated

ASPECT (ている):
{打|う}ち{上|あ}げて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ describes a launch in progress or a repeated practice, not a resulting state. For something that has already been sent up and is now in orbit, use the passive {打|う}ち{上|あ}げられて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧.

USAGE:
Sense 1 covers anything sent up into the sky by its own thrust or by an explosive charge - fireworks, rockets, satellites, signal flares.

Sense 2 is almost always expressed with the noun form ⟦{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ→打ち上げ：09795_uchiage⟧ rather than with the verb, which is why the sense 2 examples below all use the noun:
- ⟦{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ→打ち上げ：09795_uchiage⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (hold a wrap-up party)
- ⟦{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ→打ち上げ：09795_uchiage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ (go to the wrap-up party)
- ⟦{公演|こうえん}→公演：11639_kouen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ (post-performance party)
- ⟦{撮影|さつえい}→撮影：04175_satsuei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{打|う}ち{上|あ}げ (filming wrap party)
The party sense is a fixture of Japanese work and performance culture.
